Definition: from G5259 and G191; to hear under (as a subordinate), i.e. to listen attentively; by implication, to heed or conform to a command or authority:--hearken, be obedient to, obey.
BiblicalUsage: hypakoúō is a plain word for hearken, be obedient to, obey. In Matthew 8:27, the text says "that even the winds and the sea obey him!" In Mark 1:27, the text says "and they do obey him."
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that hypakoúō matters because obedience is not drudgery; it is trusting that God's way is the good way. That is why I keep this word in mind when I read those passages — it carries more than its size suggests.
RelatedEvents: Jesus Calms the Storm; Martyrdom of Stephen; Jesus Heals a Demoniac in the Capernaum Synagogue
